1.assumed: Ultraviolet wavelengths lie roughly between 10 nm and 400 nm.

2.assumed: Kirchhoff's laws are stated in terms of current, e.m.f. and p.d., not charge.

3.assumed: Snell's law uses angles from the normal: subtract boundary angles from 90°.

4.assumed: Fringe spacing x = λD/a: large λ and small a give widest fringes.

5.assumed: Braking power = loss of kinetic energy ÷ time.

6.assumed: 270° phase difference means path difference of ¾λ (or that plus whole wavelengths).

8.assumed: Current from V/R; lost volts = ε − V; r = lost volts ÷ I.

9.assumed: Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action.

10.assumed: Charge = number of electrons × e; I = Q/t with µs converted.

11.assumed: Useful power = Fh/t; input power = useful power ÷ efficiency.

12.assumed: Rotating a polarising filter in polarised light changes transmitted intensity, not frequency or speed.

13.assumed: Extension = FL/(AE): scales with L, inversely with E.

14.assumed: NTC thermistor resistance decreases (non-linearly) as temperature rises.

15.assumed: Fixed moment means F × x is constant, so x is inversely proportional to F.

16.assumed: Straight line through origin is ohmic; filament-lamp curve shows rising resistance.

17.assumed: UV photons release electrons from the zinc surface (photoelectric effect).

18.assumed: Energy = charge × p.d., charge = N × e.

19.assumed: Any wave can form stationary waves; sound is longitudinal and needs a medium, EM doesn't.

21(a).assumed: Distance is the area under a v–t graph: split into trapezium and rectangle.

21(b)(i).assumed: Acceleration is the gradient of the v–t graph.

21(b)(ii).assumed: Horizontal component T cos θ minus resistance equals ma.

22(a).assumed: Add known loads, measure compression each time, plot force vs compression; gradient = k.

22(b).assumed: Rising and slowing: kinetic energy becomes gravitational potential energy.

22(c).assumed: E = ½kx² with compression in metres.

22(d).assumed: Some elastic energy also becomes gravitational potential energy as it rises.

23(a).assumed: Force = gradient of p–t graph; third law needs equal and opposite forces.

23(b).assumed: Read momenta from graphs with sign; totals before and after must be equal.

23(c).assumed: Objects stick, so total momentum ÷ total mass gives common velocity.

23(d).assumed: Vertical motion is independent: from rest s = ½gt².

24(a).assumed: Stationary waves show fixed nodes and antinodes.

24(b)(i).assumed: Use a signal generator display, or microphone and oscilloscope with f = 1/T; reduce noise or time many cycles.

24(b)(ii)1.assumed: Fundamental between fixed ends is half a wavelength, so λ = 2L.

24(b)(ii)3.assumed: Percentage uncertainties add, doubling for a squared term; convert to absolute.

25(a).assumed: Both e.m.f. and p.d. are measured in volts (energy per unit charge).

25(b)(i).assumed: Parallel combination of wire and resistor changes; p.d. shared by resistance ratio in a divider.

25(b)(ii).assumed: In series, p.d. shares in proportion to resistance; larger total resistance means smaller current.

25(c)(i).assumed: P.d. across wires = supply − lamp p.d.; R = V/I; ρ = RA/L with mm² converted.

26(a)(i).assumed: Emission needs photon energy at least equal to the work function.

26(a)(ii).assumed: Threshold wavelength λ = hc/φ; wavelength inversely proportional to energy.

26(a)(iii).assumed: KEmax = photon energy − φ; convert to J, find v or p, then λ = h/p.

26(b)(i).assumed: Draw a straight best-fit line through the plotted points.

26(b)(ii).assumed: KEmax = hf − φ: gradient is h, intercept is −φ.
